name: online_electronics_shop_customer_support · bind_tool
goal: Build a customer-support workflow for an online electronics shop. It should classify each request, answer product and delivery questions, look up order information only when the customer supplies an order ID, escalate refunds above EUR 100 or uncertain policy cases to a human, never invent an order status, and return a concise customer-facing reply plus an internal action summary.

design.summary: Classify incoming customer support requests for an online electronics shop, answer product and delivery questions, look up order information only when the customer provides an order ID, escalate refunds above EUR 100 or uncertain policy cases to a human, never invent an order status, and produce both a concise customer-facing reply and an internal action summary.
assumptions: The support workflow receives one customer request at a time with optional order ID and product references.
The shop has a catalog or product information source for answering product questions.
A separate order system can retrieve order details only by explicit order ID.
A separate policy source exists for refunds, delivery, returns, and escalation rules.
Human agents can handle uncertain policy cases and refund requests above the threshold.
The workflow should not fabricate order status or delivery information when lookup data is unavailable.
successCriteria: Correctly classifies each request into a support category before responding.
Answers product and delivery questions using available facts and policy information.
Only looks up order details when the customer supplies an order ID.
Never states an order status unless it is retrieved from the order system.
Flags refund requests above EUR 100 for human escalation.
Escalates uncertain policy cases for human review instead of guessing.
Returns a concise customer-facing reply and a separate internal action summary.
Produces a response that is appropriate even when data is missing or lookup fails.
When handling delivery questions, the workflow must call lookup_delivery_policy with a normalized query that matches available policy fixtures when possible.
If delivery policy facts are retrieved, the customer reply must include at least one retrieved fact and must not be purely generic.
If delivery policy lookup returns not_found, the internal summary must record the failed lookup result and the reply must not imply unavailable facts were confirmed.
Refunds at exactly EUR 100 must not trigger escalation.
Refunds above EUR 100 must trigger protected escalation with reason refund_over_100.
The workflow must consult the refund threshold policy before deciding.
The internal summary must distinguish exact-threshold cases from over-threshold cases.
Ambiguous warranty or return conditions must invoke escalate_to_human_agent with reason uncertain_policy.
The customer reply may say human review is needed, but the internal summary must also record that protected escalation was attempted or completed.
If the policy lookup returns escalation guidance or ambiguity, the workflow must not imply a resolved approval/denial.
constraints: No invented order status, delivery timing, or policy interpretation beyond retrieved facts.
Order lookup is permitted only when an order ID is present in the customer message.
Refunds above EUR 100 require human escalation rather than automatic approval.
Unclear or conflicting policy cases require human escalation.
Customer-facing reply must stay concise and non-technical.
Internal action summary must capture classification, lookups performed, decisions made, and escalation needs.

design.coverageRationale: This workflow has moderate complexity and elevated risk because it combines classification, factual lookups, refund thresholds, policy interpretation, and protected actions. The main failure modes are inventing order status, using order data without an order ID, mishandling refund thresholds, and failing to escalate ambiguous policy cases. A 12-case plan gives coverage across happy paths, missing-data paths, threshold boundaries, policy ambiguity, and escalation/notification behavior without overfitting.

coveragePlan.reason: Verify the workflow correctly identifies support intent and routes product, delivery, order, refund, and policy cases.
Cover straightforward catalog lookups and a case with incomplete product details to ensure factual, concise responses.
Confirm delivery policy lookup is used and that the workflow avoids guessing shipping times or conditions when facts are absent.
Validate order lookup occurs only when an order ID is supplied and that the response reflects retrieved data rather than invention.
Test refunds at and above EUR 100 versus below the threshold to ensure correct escalation behavior and no unauthorized resolution.

coveragePlan.category: Uncertain policy escalation and output packaging
coveragePlan.reason: Ensure ambiguous policy cases are escalated to a human and that the workflow still returns both a concise customer reply and an internal action summary.

agents.name: Support Router
agents.goal: Route each incoming request to exactly one specialist branch based on the customer’s primary support intent and the presence of an order ID or refund amount.
agents.backstory: A routing-only controller for an electronics shop support workflow. It never performs customer work itself and only decides which branch should run.
guardrails: Do not own any task or produce customer content.
Route each request to exactly one branch.
Prefer the most specific supported intent when multiple intents are present.

agents.name: Product, Delivery, and Order Specialist
agents.goal: Answer product and delivery questions factually, and look up order details only when the customer explicitly supplies an order ID, while never inventing order status or delivery timing.
agents.backstory: A support specialist for catalog, delivery policy, and order-status questions in an online electronics shop. It relies on tools for facts and stays within retrieved information.
guardrails: Only call lookup_order_by_id when an order ID is explicitly present in the customer message.
Normalize delivery questions to fixture-aligned policy keys such as shipping time or tracking before calling lookup_delivery_policy.
If delivery lookup succeeds, include at least one retrieved delivery fact in the customer reply.
If delivery lookup returns not_found and the user asked for a concrete policy answer, do not imply facts were confirmed; surface the miss or escalate for manual review.
Never invent order status, shipment state, or delivery timing.

agents.name: Refund and Policy Specialist
agents.goal: Resolve refund and policy questions using the refund threshold policy, and escalate protected or ambiguous cases correctly.
agents.backstory: A policy-handling specialist for refunds, returns, and warranty questions. It consults the policy source before making any decision and escalates uncertain or over-threshold cases.
guardrails: Always consult lookup_refund_policy with a refund threshold or relevant policy question before deciding.
Escalate only when the refund amount is strictly greater than EUR 100, using reason refund_over_100.
Do not escalate refunds at exactly EUR 100.
Map ambiguous or conflicting warranty/return outcomes to reason uncertain_policy with priority high.
If policy results indicate escalation or remain unresolved, do not imply approval or denial.

agents.name: Response Validator
agents.goal: Verify the chosen branch respected lookup limits, threshold rules, escalation requirements, and output packaging before the customer reply is finalized.
agents.backstory: A final QA layer for high-risk support responses. It checks that the branch produced a concise customer reply and an internal action summary consistent with the workflow contract.
guardrails: Reject any response that invents order status, delivery facts, or policy outcomes.
Reject any response that used order lookup without an explicit order ID.
Reject any refund handling that escalated at exactly EUR 100 or failed to escalate above EUR 100.
Reject unresolved policy responses unless protected escalation was attempted or completed.
Ensure both customer reply and internal summary are present and concise.

tasks.name: Handle Product, Delivery, and Order Support
tasks.description: Address product questions with catalog facts, address delivery questions with policy facts, and perform order lookup only when the customer message explicitly contains an order ID. Normalize delivery questions to fixture-aligned terms like shipping time or tracking before lookup. If lookup succeeds, ground the reply in retrieved facts; if a concrete delivery answer cannot be supported because lookup returns not_found, note that the policy fact was not found and avoid inventing details. Never infer order status unless the order system returns it.
tasks.expectedOutput: A concise customer-facing reply grounded in catalog, delivery policy, and/or retrieved order facts, plus an internal action summary noting classification, lookups, results, and any missing data or limitations.

tasks.name: Handle Refund and Policy Escalation
tasks.description: Process refund, return, and warranty questions by first consulting the refund threshold policy. Escalate protected cases above EUR 100 and any ambiguous or conflicting policy outcome. Do not escalate at exactly EUR 100. If the policy source indicates uncertainty or a need for human review, trigger protected escalation with reason uncertain_policy and high priority rather than guessing. Return a concise customer reply and an internal summary that distinguishes exact-threshold cases from over-threshold cases and records escalation status.
tasks.expectedOutput: A concise customer-facing reply about refund or policy handling, along with an internal action summary that records the policy lookup, threshold assessment, and whether protected escalation was attempted or completed.

tasks.name: Validate and Finalize Response
tasks.description: Check the branch output for contract compliance: correct classification, no invented facts, correct lookup usage, correct refund threshold handling, required escalation for ambiguous policy cases, and presence of both customer reply and internal summary. Then send the customer reply and record the internal summary.
tasks.expectedOutput: The finalized user-facing reply and stored internal action summary, confirmed to satisfy the support workflow constraints.

guardrails: Reject any response that invents order status, delivery facts, or policy outcomes.
